introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Substitute $u = \cos 3x$. Then $\dfrac{du}{dx} = -3\sin 3x$, so $\sin 3x \, dx = -\dfrac{1}{3}\,du$.

Limits: $x = 0 \Rightarrow u = \cos 0 = 1$; $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow u = \cos\pi = -1$.

$$\int_0^{\pi/3} \cos^4 3x \sin 3x \, dx = \int_{1}^{-1} u^4 \left(-\frac13\right) du = \frac13 \int_{-1}^{1} u^4 \, du = \frac13\left[\frac{u^5}{5}\right]_{-1}^{1} = \frac13 \cdot \frac{1 - (-1)}{5} = \frac{2}{15}.$$

$$\boxed{\int_0^{\pi/3} \cos^4 3x \sin 3x \, dx = \frac{2}{15}}$$

**Check** by the reverse chain rule: $F(x) = -\dfrac{\cos^5 3x}{15}$ has $F'(x) = -\dfrac{5\cos^4 3x \cdot (-3\sin 3x)}{15} = \cos^4 3x \sin 3x$. Then $F\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = -\dfrac{(-1)^5}{15} = \dfrac{1}{15}$ and $F(0) = -\dfrac{1}{15}$, so the integral is $\dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{2}{15}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the volume of the solid generated when the curve $y = x^3$ is rotated completely about the $x$-axis between the ordinates $x = 0$ and $x = 3$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A thin disc at position $x$ has radius $y = x^3$ and thickness $dx$, so its volume is $\pi y^2\,dx$. The volume of revolution about the $x$-axis is

$$V = \pi \int_0^3 y^2 \, dx = \pi \int_0^3 (x^3)^2 \, dx = \pi \int_0^3 x^6 \, dx = \pi\left[\frac{x^7}{7}\right]_0^3 = \frac{3^7 \pi}{7} = \frac{2187\pi}{7}.$$

$$\boxed{V = \frac{2187\pi}{7} \approx 981.5 \text{ cubic units}}$$

(Numerically $2187/7 = 312.43$ and $312.43 \times \pi = 981.52$. No units are given in the question, so the answer is in cubic units.)
